suburb.house-cleaning-north-stubville.intro: North Stubville sits along the ridge above the fixture line, and it's one of the districts our crews know best. The neighbourhood grew up around wide corner lots and deep front porches, and most owners here are more particular about their yards than their floors — which is exactly the kind of house we like showing up to.
suburb.house-cleaning-north-stubville.homes: The mock bungalows through Assertion Acres and Mock Meadows date to the early fixture era: one story, original hardwood under decades of wax, and closets sized for a smaller wardrobe than anyone owns today. Newer construction in Stub Village Estates and Canned Creek runs larger, with open kitchens and engineered flooring that scratches if it's mopped wrong. Placeholder Heights and Fixture Court split the difference — mid-size ranch homes with finished basements that trap whatever the ground floor tracks downstairs. We adjust our approach street by street rather than running one routine across the whole area.
suburb.house-cleaning-north-stubville.local: Six months of test season keep North Stubville's original single-pane windows sealed shut, and fixture dust builds up on the deep porch rails and sills faster than most owners notice until it's tracked indoors on shoes. The older hardwood in Assertion Acres also holds onto grit in its gaps, so a surface pass just pushes it around instead of lifting it out. We work the window tracks and baseboards on every visit and go after the floor seams with a different tool than we use on the newer builds.

suburb.cleaning-services-mock-hollow.intro: Mock Hollow's stub-frame duplexes sit close enough together that a cleaning crew has to work quietly, and we've built our schedule there around that. It's a smaller footprint than North Stubville, but the shared walls and tight setbacks mean the little things — a scuffed shared entry, a dusty shared vent — matter more to how the whole street looks.
suburb.cleaning-services-mock-hollow.homes: Mock Hollow Commons and Mock Hollow Terrace are both built to the same duplex pattern: narrow galley kitchens, laminate counters original to the fixture era, and shared stairwells that see twice the foot traffic of a single-family entry. Bedrooms upstairs run small, so closets and under-bed space get used hard, and that's where lint and fixture dust collect fastest. Because the units share a wall, sound and vibration from one side loosens dust into the other, which is not something North Stubville's detached bungalows ever have to deal with.
suburb.cleaning-services-mock-hollow.local: The shared walls and stairwells in Mock Hollow Commons and Mock Hollow Terrace mean dust and fixture-season grit move between units in a way a standalone house never sees, so a clean on one side doesn't hold if the shared entry is neglected.
